title: Stack avionics modules and covers on standoffs
instruction: Seat each gold module on its four standoffs, then the blue cover flat on top. Centre both over the standoffs within 5 mm, long sides along the deck's long side.
context: A 1 g bench analogue of a step in spacecraft avionics integration: a board is seated on its chassis standoffs, long side along the deck, then its cover is fitted on top, one assembly per arm. Electrical and electronic equipment assemblers (O*NET 51-2022) do this step on Earth every day. The fixed posts set the tolerance physically, not only the rubric. Within 9 to 13 mm of the centre, depending on direction, the module rests level on the posts; further off it tips onto the deck, and turned 90 degrees it cannot rest on all four. The cover is judged from the deck centre, the chassis datum a real cover is fastened to, so any error in the module under it eats into the cover's 5 mm. Each module starts with its long side across the table, so the arm must turn it 90 degrees on the way. No fasteners, connectors or microgravity are claimed.
setup: Station table, both lanes. Frame: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left, z up, metres; table top at z 0.7475; arm bases at (0, 0.305, 0.75) and (0, -0.305, 0.75). Positions are given for the left lane; the right lane is its mirror image (y becomes -y), and every object name carries a left_ or right_ prefix. Every object is a rigid matte primitive with static friction 1.2 and dynamic friction 1.0; fixed objects have no mass and cannot move. Fixed, per lane (7 objects): the deck, a box 140 x 100 x 4 mm, dark grey (sRGB 0.20, 0.20, 0.22), long side along x, centred at (0.160, 0.300), top face at z 0.7515; four standoffs (standoff_1 to standoff_4), cylinders 8 mm in diameter and 20 mm tall, light grey (sRGB 0.80, 0.80, 0.80), standing on the deck at x 0.130 and 0.190 and y 0.280 and 0.320, the corners of a 60 x 40 mm rectangle centred on the deck, tops at z 0.7715; the module pad, a box 80 x 80 x 2 mm, white (sRGB 0.95, 0.95, 0.93), centred at (0.360, 0.300); the cover pad, a box 100 x 70 x 2 mm, long side along x, white (sRGB 0.95, 0.95, 0.93), centred at (0.290, 0.420); both pad tops at z 0.7495. Free, per lane (2 objects): the module, a box 70 x 50 x 30 mm, 100 g, gold (sRGB 0.85, 0.70, 0.25), resting on the module pad with its centre at (0.360, 0.300, 0.7645), turned 90 degrees so its long side lies along y, across the table; the cover, a box 90 x 60 x 20 mm, 80 g, dark blue (sRGB 0.10, 0.15, 0.45), resting on the cover pad with its centre at (0.290, 0.420, 0.7595), long side along x. In all, 14 fixed and 4 free objects. A module with its long side along x covers the post pattern with 1 mm to spare beyond each post's outer edge; its 50 mm width is less than the 52 mm between the posts' inner faces along x, so a module turned 90 degrees cannot rest on all four posts: centred within 1 mm along x it drops between them onto the deck, otherwise it catches one pair and tips about 25 degrees. The pads are at least 36 mm from the deck and 45 mm from each other, and the two lanes are 0.6 m apart. Goal per lane: the module centred on the pattern at (0.160, 0.300), long side along x, bottom on the post tops at z 0.7715; the cover centred over the pattern at (0.160, 0.300), long side along x, bottom on the module's top at z 0.8015. To build it: two plywood or MDF decks 140 x 100 x 4 mm taped to the table, each with four 8 mm hardwood dowels cut 20 mm tall and glued upright through a drilled jig so their tops are coplanar within 1 mm; two wooden blocks 70 x 50 x 30 mm painted gold and weighted to about 100 g; two wooden blocks 90 x 60 x 20 mm painted dark blue, about 80 g; white card pads at the stated centres.
scoring: End state only, judged per lane after the arms stop, from a top photo, a steel ruler and a phone level. Each lane scores 0, 0.15, 0.30 or 0.50, and the task score is the sum of the two lanes: 0, 0.15, 0.30, 0.45, 0.50, 0.60, 0.65, 0.80 or 1.0. Module seated, 0.30: a gold module at rest (moving under 10 mm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s) with a 70 x 50 mm face down and tilted 5 degrees or less, its bottom face within 2 mm of the standoff tops (z 0.7715), its centre within 5 mm of the pattern centre (0.160, 0.300 or -0.300) and its long side within 5 degrees of x, either way round. Module roughly seated, 0.15: the same rest, tilt and height tests, but the centre 5 to 10 mm off or the long side 5 to 15 degrees off x. Most such modules rest level on the posts; at 10 to 15 degrees of yaw one more than 5 to 7 mm off tips and scores 0. Cover, plus 0.20, only on a seated (0.30) module: a blue cover at rest, tilted 5 degrees or less, its bottom face within 2 mm of the module's top face (z 0.8015 for a seated module), its centre within 5 mm of the pattern centre, not of the module's centre, and its long side within 5 degrees of x, either way round. The cover is judged from the same datum as the module, so a module 3 mm off leaves a cover centred on it only 2 mm more in that direction. Any other module state gives the lane 0. That includes a module on the deck between or beside the posts (bottom below z 0.7695), tipped off the posts (beyond 9 to 13 mm off, depending on direction, a module tips 20 to 50 degrees onto the deck), turned 90 degrees (it cannot rest on all four posts: centred within 1 mm it drops between them, otherwise it catches one pair and tips about 25 degrees), more than 10 mm off or more than 15 degrees turned, standing on a side or an end, tilted more than 5 degrees, on a pad or the table, still moving or turning, or above post height, for example on a cover. Any other cover state adds nothing. That includes a cover on the posts (the module then cannot be at post height, so the lane scores 0), on the deck, a pad or the table, tilted more than 5 degrees, turned more than 5 degrees, more than 5 mm off the pattern centre, or on a module that scores only 0.15. The two modules are identical and so are the two covers, so either module may seat on either pattern and either cover may cap it; each lane counts once, at its best module. Success, which ends the trial, is both lanes at 0.50 held for 1 s. The start layout scores 0. The decks, standoffs and pads are fixed in simulation; on real arms a standoff bent, loosened or moved more than 1 mm, or a moved deck, scores 0 for that lane. The simulated scorer reads object poses and velocities only and cannot see the grippers, so a module held in place on the posts scores like a released one; real trials are judged after both arms are parked clear of the parts. Judging on the real rig: module and cover offsets with the ruler from the deck edges (the pattern centre is the deck centre), level with the phone (5 degrees over 70 mm is 6 mm end to end). In simulation every test uses the part's centre and quaternion, and an exact limit counts (0.1 mm and 0.1 mrad epsilon).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand each module back on its module pad with its long side across the table, and each cover on its cover pad with its long side along x; the decks, standoffs and pads do not move. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the layout and the open-loop demo depend on it.
fidelity: Approximate: no fasteners, connectors, harness or thermal interface; the module rests on four posts and the cover on the module, held by gravity and friction (one matte material, 1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Standoffs, decks and pads are static colliders that cannot bend or shift in simulation; the real-world rule covers that case. Both parts are uniform boxes, so either large face down counts; a real board has one correct face. Earth gravity on a bench.
